To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light-like tetragon for three dimensional pure and matter Chern-Simons theory, when evaluated within dimensional regularization with the dimensional reduction scheme, respects maximal transcendentancy and matches the corresponding scattering amplitude both at the level of the divergent and the finite part.
the two-loop light like Wilson loop in the ABJM theory is finite and that its finite part matches the finite part of the four-point amplitude.
the two-loop lightlike Wilson loop in ABJM and the four-point amplitude are related by the duality of the theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new, more precise, and more complete calculation of the Wilson loop, which is also a new and more precise calculation of the amplitude.
the study of the two-loop tetragonal Wilson loops in three-dimensional pure Chern-Simsons theory and $ \mathscr{N} $ = 6 Chern-Symons-matter theory.
the computation of the light-like Wilson loops of the ABJM theory in the planar limit, at one- and two-loop order.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the case of the tetragonal light-like Wilson loop and the four-point amplitude of $ \mathcal {N}=6 $ Chern-Simons matter theory, dimensional regularization with dimensional-reduction scheme is equivalent to dimensional regularization with the minimal subtraction scheme.
the Wilson loop is the scattering amplitude, and vice versa.
the Wilson loop and the four-point amplitude are related by a duality transformation, and the maximal transcendentality property is preserved in both sides of the duality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two-loop lightlike Wilson loop is a maximally transcendentally correct quantity, which is a remarkable property.
, at the perturbative level, the light-like Wilson loop and the scattering amplitude of the ABJM theory have the same structure.
the Wilson loop is not a Wilson loop, but a scattering amplitude in disguise.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Wilson loops in ABJ(M) theory, and more generally in Chern-Simons theories, are not only a useful tool to study the dynamics of the theory but also a valuable tool to test and improve the current understanding of the structure of gauge and gravity theories in the light-like limit.

the two-loop tetragonal Wilson loops in ABJ(M) theories, as well as in pure CS, are not only finite and ultraviolet finite but also maximal transcendental, in dimensional regularization with dimensional-reduction.
the Wilson loop and the scattering amplitude are not independent objects in ABJM and its generalization.
